definition: See Knowledge Distillation — the general process of transferring capabilities from a larger model to a smaller, more efficient one.
details: The term is often used interchangeably with knowledge distillation in the context of building smaller production-ready LLMs from larger frontier models.

explainer.lead: The general process of transferring capabilities from a larger model to a smaller, more efficient one, often used interchangeably with knowledge distillation. It matters for building smaller production-ready LLMs from larger frontier models.

tiers.eli5: It is like a student learning to imitate a expert teacher and picking up much of the skill in a smaller package.
tiers.practitioner: Teams distill larger frontier models into smaller models suited to production. A pitfall is expecting the smaller model to retain every capability of the teacher.
tiers.paperLevel: Transfer of capabilities from a larger model to a smaller, more efficient one; the term is often used interchangeably with knowledge distillation.

explainer.example: A smaller production LLM is built by transferring capabilities from a larger frontier model.
